newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ govt partners consider extra clauses in deal.
newsitem.headline: NZ govt partners consider extra clauses in deal.

text.p: The conservative National Party and nationalist New Zealand First on Thursday were considering the detail of an addition to their coalition agreement covering issues settled in their coalition talks but not included in a document released last week.

The document, or "addendum" is expected to include consideration of compensation for people who have contracted hepatitis C or HIV from contaminated blood supplies, more funding for the Commissioner for Children, and consideration of supporting a class action for victims of nuclear testing on Christmas Island.
It could also include details of resourcing of NZ First which the main opposition Labour Party said was raised during its unsuccessful coalition talks with NZ First.
National's caucus met to be briefed on the addendum, while NZ First caucus members were being contacted to discuss its contents, NZPA reported.
Spokespeople for Prime Minister Jim Bolger and Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters said the addendum would be released either late Thursday or early Friday.
Free-market Act New Zealand's caucus of eight MPs has withheld support for the government on confidence issues until all details of the coalition agreement are made public.
National's caucus was also due to consider the election of a new chief whip to replace list MP Roger Sowry, who was promoted to Welfare Minister in the coalition cabinet.

The government is yet to say when it will release the details of the areas of responsibility of the new Treasurer's job, held by NZ First leader Wisnton Peters, and the existing Finance Minister Bill Birch. A government spokesman said the details had been finalised.
